developments: US producer prices rose 0.3% in October, below the 0.4% forecast, and bitcoin jumped to $70,190 on Kraken within the hour of the 13:30 UK release.
The bounce did not hold: after Wall Street opened, the Nasdaq fell about 1.6% on Nvidia's leadership turmoil, the 10-year yield touched 5.16%, and bitcoin slipped back to about $68,700 by 16:45 UK.
Final figures put Thursday's US spot bitcoin ETF outflows at $284 million, a sixth straight day, with BlackRock's IBIT losing $204 million, according to SoSoValue data.
briefing.changed: This morning bitcoin was near $68,900 after the overnight flush to $67,500. A softer PPI gave a brief lift above $70,000, but US stocks turned lower and bitcoin gave it all back, so the picture is little changed: still risk-off, still below $70,000. The US military has denied Iran's radar-strike claim, which takes some edge off the geopolitical worry. Zcash has held up better, back near $954.
briefing.question: With producer inflation at 6.5% and the 10-year above 5%, does a softer monthly PPI change anything for a December Fed hike, or does the market keep pricing a larger move?
briefing.watch: The US close at 21:00 UK and tonight's Friday ETF flow figures. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Bitcoin's PPI bounce fades as tech sell-off drags Wall Street
lead.standfirst: A softer-than-expected US producer price reading lifted bitcoin briefly above $70,000, but the gain vanished as Nvidia's leadership crisis pulled the Nasdaq lower and Treasury yields climbed.
body: Bitcoin rose to $70,190 on Kraken shortly after 13:30 UK on Friday, when the US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that producer prices for final demand rose 0.3% in October, below the 0.4% economists had forecast. About $39 million of short positions were liquidated within an hour of the release, crypto.news reported, citing CoinGlass.

The relief was short-lived. US stocks opened higher at 14:30 UK and then turned lower, with the Nasdaq down about 1.6% and the S&P 500 down about 0.8% by late morning in New York, Yahoo Finance reported. Nvidia shares swung sharply after Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive, and the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.16%, its highest since October.
Bitcoin slid back to about $68,000 in the hour after the open and traded near $68,700 at 16:45 UK, according to Kraken data, down about 3.7% on the day.

The annual picture gave little comfort. Producer inflation reached 6.5% over 12 months, the largest annual increase since November 2022, and core prices rose 5.0%. Traders remain divided between a quarter-point and half-point Fed hike in December, crypto.news reported.

Selling from US spot bitcoin ETFs also continued. Thursday's final figures showed $284 million of net outflows, the sixth day in a row, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for $204 million, according to SoSoValue data reported by PANews.
Friday's ETF flows and the US close at 21:00 UK are next. The Fed's December decision is due on 9 December.

headline: A softer US PPI lifted bitcoin briefly above $70,000, but a Nvidia-led tech sell-off and 5.16% Treasury yields pushed it back to about $68,700. ETF outflows reached a sixth day, while the US denied Iran's radar-strike claim.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, afternoon edition. US producer prices rose zero point three percent in October, a little softer than expected, and bitcoin briefly jumped above seventy thousand dollars just after half past one. The bounce faded once Wall Street opened: the Nasdaq fell about one and a half percent as Nvidia's leadership turmoil hit tech, and the ten-year Treasury yield touched five point one six percent. Bitcoin is back near sixty-eight thousand seven hundred dollars. Spot bitcoin funds lost two hundred and eighty-four million dollars on Thursday, a sixth day of outflows. The US has denied Iran's claim to have hit a radar in Bahrain. Zcash is steadier, near nine hundred and fifty dollars. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Bitcoin's jump above $70,000 on soft PPI fades after the US open
stories.why: Since this morning's $68,900, bitcoin rose to $70,190 on Kraken in the hour after the 13:30 UK PPI release, then fell to about $68,040 after the 14:30 US open and traded near $68,700 at 16:45 UK, down about 3.7% on the day. crypto.news, citing CoinGlass, said about $39 million of shorts were liquidated after the data and $1.42 billion of positions over 24 hours, 83% of them longs.

note.read: The failed push through $70,000 suggests sellers are still in control and that bitcoin is trading with US tech stocks and yields rather than on its own news.
note.alt: Friday afternoon liquidity is thin; the reversal may reflect position-squaring before the weekend more than fresh selling.
note.change: A close back above $70,000 with ETF outflows stopping would weaken the risk-off read; a break below this morning's $67,500 low would strengthen it.

stories.title: US producer prices rise 0.3% in October, softer than forecast
stories.why: Final demand PPI rose 0.3% against 0.4% expected, with core also up 0.3%, in line. Over 12 months PPI rose 6.5% (forecast 6.6%), the biggest annual rise since November 2022, and core rose 5.0%. September was revised to 1.4%. It eases this week's inflation scare a little, after Tuesday's hot CPI.
stories.caveat: The BLS release page could not be loaded directly; figures are from StockTitan and crypto.news, which agree.

note.read: A one-tenth miss on the monthly figure is small next to 6.5% annual producer inflation; it does little to take a December hike off the table.
note.alt: If the softer monthly pace continues into November data, markets may start to price a smaller December move.
note.change: Fed officials signalling a quarter-point rather than a half-point hike, or CME FedWatch odds shifting that way.

stories.title: Nasdaq falls about 1.6% as Nvidia turmoil and 5.16% yields weigh
stories.why: US stocks opened higher, then reversed: by late morning in New York the Nasdaq was down about 1.6%, the S&P 500 about 0.8% and the Dow 0.2%, Yahoo Finance reported. Nvidia fell as much as 14% at the open after Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO, with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. The 10-year yield hit 5.16% and the VIX rose above 20. Bitcoin has tracked the Nasdaq lower.
stories.caveat: Yahoo's live blog gave slightly different index figures in its text and quote table; the numbers are approximate.

note.read: Leadership risk at the market's biggest AI stock, on top of 5% yields, is a fresh headwind for risk assets including bitcoin.
note.alt: Nvidia recovered part of its opening drop, and the major indices are still on course for weekly gains, so this may be a one-day shock.
note.change: Nvidia's results on Tuesday 17 November after the US close, and whether the 10-year yield falls back below 5%.

stories.title: Thursday's ETF outflows finalised at $284 million, sixth day in a row
stories.why: This morning's early figure was $47.7 million with BlackRock and Fidelity still to report. SoSoValue data, reported by PANews, now puts Thursday's total net outflow at $284 million, with BlackRock's IBIT losing $204 million. Cointelegraph had already counted more than $2 billion leaving IBIT over the nine sessions to Wednesday, so Thursday extends that run to ten.
stories.caveat: Farside's own Thursday total could not be checked; the SoSoValue figure is reported through a single aggregator.

stories.title: US denies Iran's Bahrain radar-strike claim, says it downed two drones
stories.why: This morning the claim was unverified. The US military has since denied that any radar was hit, saying it shot down two one-way attack drones launched by the Revolutionary Guards towards Bahrain with no harm done, AP reported via Yahoo. Oil was little changed near $89 after Thursday's spike, per Yahoo Finance. The denial lowers the immediate escalation risk, though the Strait of Hormuz standoff continues.

stories.title: Zcash recovers to about $954, outperforming bitcoin
stories.why: ZEC rose from about $938 this morning to a high of $992 on Kraken before settling near $954 at 16:45 UK, roughly flat on the day while bitcoin is down about 3.7%. No Zcash-specific news explained the move.

stories.title: Bitcoin treasury firm Nakamoto owes Kraken more than its market value
stories.why: Nakamoto owes Kraken 165 million USDT, backed by 3,030 pledged BTC worth about $208 million (roughly 126% of the debt) at $69,000, CoinDesk calculated. Its market value is about $104 million. A 12 November amendment pushed $60 million of repayments to December 2027. It shows how a falling bitcoin price squeezes leveraged treasury companies.
stories.caveat: The loan's margin-call threshold is not disclosed.

stories.title: SpaceX–Tesla merger talks would combine about 30,220 bitcoin
stories.why: Bloomberg reported that SpaceX and Tesla are in merger talks, with an announcement possible as soon as December, CoinDesk said. Together they hold about 30,220 BTC (about $2.1 billion). A deal would combine existing holdings and needs no new buying.

explained.title: Producer prices versus consumer prices
body: The Producer Price Index (PPI) measures what businesses receive for their goods and services, while the Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures what households pay. Because firms often pass costs on, PPI is watched as an early signal of where consumer inflation may head.
Markets react to the surprise, not the level. Today's 0.3% monthly rise beat the 0.4% forecast, which is why bitcoin jumped, even though the 6.5% annual rate is the highest since 2022.

investigating: Does the 5.16% 10-year yield push markets towards a half-point December hike? Evidence: CME FedWatch odds and Fed speakers over the next week.
Did ETF outflows continue on Friday for a seventh day? Evidence: Farside and SoSoValue figures tonight.
